title: Salvation by Grace
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Salvation by grace means that sinners are saved by God’s undeserved favor through faith in Jesus Christ, not by works, merit, religious achievement, personal effort, or self-improvement. Grace is God’s saving gift to the guilty, helpless, and undeserving, given through Christ and received by faith.
summary: Salvation by grace means that sinners are saved by God’s undeserved favor through faith in Jesus Christ, not by works, merit, religious achievement, personal effort, or self-improvement. Grace is God’s saving gift to the guilty, helpless, and undeserving, given through Christ and received by faith.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the full revelation and gift of God’s saving grace. Through His death and resurrection, sinners are forgiven, justified, made alive, and brought near to God. Salvation is by grace because Christ has accomplished what sinners could never accomplish for themselves.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Salvation does not begin with human strength, wisdom, morality, or desire. Scripture teaches that sinners are spiritually dead, enslaved to sin, guilty before God, and unable to make themselves righteous. People may try to improve themselves, hide their guilt, compare themselves to others, perform religious duties, or prove they are worthy, but none of these can remove sin or reconcile a person to God.

Grace means that God saves because of His mercy and goodness, not because sinners have earned His favor. God does not look at fallen people and find hidden merit that deserves salvation. He acts in love toward the undeserving and gives what could never be purchased, achieved, or demanded. Salvation is a gift, not a wage.

This grace comes through Jesus Christ. God justifies sinners through faith in Christ, apart from works of the law. Jesus bore the guilt of His people, fulfilled righteousness, conquered death, and opened the way for sinners to be forgiven and made new. Grace does not ignore sin; grace answers sin through the cross and resurrection of Christ.

Salvation by grace destroys pride and despair at the same time. It destroys pride because no one can boast before God as though they saved themselves. It destroys despair because no sinner is saved by being strong enough, clean enough, religious enough, or worthy enough. The hope of salvation rests not in the sinner’s record, but in God’s grace given in Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people live under the crushing weight of trying to become acceptable to God. Some try to earn His love through good behavior, ministry activity, religious performance, recovery progress, or comparison with others. Others believe their failures, addictions, shame, sins, or repeated setbacks have made them too far gone to be saved. Salvation by grace speaks to both errors with one glorious truth: salvation is God’s gift in Christ, not the sinner’s achievement.

This doctrine keeps the Gospel free from pride, manipulation, and despair. It protects the church from preaching self-rescue in Christian language. It reminds the strong that they have nothing to boast in, and it tells the broken that grace is not reserved for people who already have themselves together. The grace that saves also teaches, changes, and restores, but it begins with God’s mercy, not human worthiness.

studySections.heading: Discipleship & Application
studySections.content: Stop trying to stand before God on the basis of your own record. Come to Christ empty-handed, trusting His finished work instead of your performance, feelings, promises, or progress. Let grace humble you, comfort you, and teach you to obey from gratitude rather than fear. When you serve others, speak the same grace clearly: sinners are not saved by cleaning themselves up for God, but by coming to Christ who saves, cleanses, restores, and makes them new.
